body: Blocking issue: this default-path fallback uses `os.path.*`, but `engine.py` does not import `os`. Because `_run_pre_compaction_extraction()` swallows exceptions, `LCM_EXTRACTION_ENABLED=true` with the default/empty `LCM_EXTRACTION_OUTPUT_PATH` turns into a silent no-op instead of writing to `~/.hermes/lcm-extractions/`. I reproduced this locally and got `name 'os' is not defined` from this path.

This recovery logic is treating a normal post-compaction state as corruption. After `compress()`, the store still contains the original raw messages, so `store_count` will legitimately be greater than the shortened in-memory cursor. Advancing the cursor to `store_count` causes new appended turns to be skipped entirely. That matches the failures in `test_ingest_after_compaction` and `test_multiple_compactions`.

This sanitization changes query semantics, not just safety. Stripping `"` means an exact phrase query like `"vendoring external"` becomes a plain token search before hitting FTS, which is why the phrase-relevance test regresses. If you want to harden MATCH input, preserve valid quoted phrases and reject/escape only the dangerous syntax instead of flattening the whole query.

This currently raises during FTS bootstrap/rebuild, which can prevent the store from initializing at all. The PR description says low disk should degrade cleanly to LIKE search, but this path turns it into a startup failure unless a higher layer catches and downgrades the error. That fallback path does not seem to exist here.

I don't think this check is buying much security as written. The backup destination is always constructed under `backup_root / "backups" / "lcm"`, so comparing `db_path.resolve()` against `backup_root.resolve()` does not meaningfully validate the final write target. In the common case where the database lives outside `hermes_home`, this just silently falls back to `db_path.parent`, which changes behavior without really addressing traversal. If you want a real guard here, validate the resolved `backup_path` after it is constructed, not the source DB path ancestry.

This rewrite updates only `content`. The original `token_estimate` is left intact, so any retention/footprint reporting based on stored token totals will still count the row as if it contained the full giant blob. That undercuts the operator-facing value of transcript GC. Please either recompute `token_estimate` from the placeholder here, or introduce a separate retained-footprint field and make the reporting path use that instead.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Set active session before current-scope grep check**

This test now calls `lcm_grep` with `session_scope` set to `current`, but the fixture keeps `engine._session_id` at `"test-session"` while all seeded data is written under `"mixed-session"`. In this setup `lcm_grep` will search the active session only and return no matches, so the assertions about discord/telegram filtering cannot hold. Update the test setup to switch the active session to `mixed-session` before invoking the tool.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Activate unknown-session before current-scope grep call**

After changing this invocation to `session_scope: "current"`, the test still seeds messages/summaries in `"unknown-session"` while the fixture’s active session remains `"test-session"`. That means `lcm_grep` is scoped away from the inserted rows and will produce empty results, so the source-filter assertions can’t pass. Set `engine._session_id` to `unknown-session` (or seed under the active session) before this call.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Order LIKE fallback rows before applying SQL LIMIT**

The new `LIMIT ?` in `MessageStore._search_like` truncates candidates before Python applies `_fallback_result_sort_key`, and this SQL has no `ORDER BY`. For LIKE-fallback queries (e.g., emoji/CJK) with more than `fetch_limit` matches, recency/relevance/hybrid can now return the wrong top-`limit` rows because only the first window is considered (for example, 120 matching rows with `limit=5` returns rows from the first 50, not the newest/best overall). Apply a sort-aligned `ORDER BY` (or iterative paging) before limiting to preserve search result correctness.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Move SummaryDAG source filter ahead of SQL LIMIT**

In `SummaryDAG._search_like`, SQL `LIMIT ?` is applied before `_node_matches_source` filters by descendant message source, so source-constrained fallback searches can return empty/underfilled results when matching-source nodes are outside the first fetch window. This is reproducible with emoji fallback: if matching source lineage starts after the first 50 rows, `search(..., source=..., limit=5)` returns 0 despite many valid matches. Include the source constraint in SQL selection or continue paging until enough source-matching nodes are collected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid capping DAG search before source-filtered hits are found**

In `SummaryDAG.search`, the new cap is enforced using `scanned_rows` from raw FTS rows, but `source` filtering is applied afterwards in Python, so the loop can terminate before collecting enough eligible nodes. With `sort="relevance"` and a sparse source (e.g., many higher-ranked non-matching nodes first), this now returns too few/zero results even when plenty of matching nodes exist later in the ranked stream; this is a regression from the previous paging behavior and breaks source-scoped recall.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp first FTS page to the candidate cap**

`candidate_cap` is computed but never applied to the initial `fetch_limit`, so the first query can still request far more rows than the cap allows (e.g., precise query with `limit=1000` yields `fetch_limit=10000` while cap is `5000`). Because the cap check runs only after fetching, this defeats the stated hard bound and still permits oversized scans on large-limit calls; the same pattern exists in both store and DAG search loops.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle unbound sessions explicitly in retention scan**

When `engine._session_id` is empty (for example, right after process start before any session binds), this new early return forces an empty analysis result even if the database already contains sessions. That now drives `/lcm doctor retention` down the `"no stored sessions found"` path, which is factually incorrect and can mislead operators into thinking retention state is empty. Please return a distinct "unbound" result/status instead of reusing the empty-database shape.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Join FTS rows using the actual message primary key**

The new `lcm_doctor` query joins `messages_fts.rowid` to `messages.id`, but the `messages` table key is `store_id` (see `MessageStore._init_db`), so this SQL raises `OperationalError: no such column: messages.id` whenever `lcm_doctor` runs. In practice this makes the `fts_index_sync` check always report `fail` instead of giving a real sync signal for any session.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match full field name in unbound status assertion**

This assertion is too broad and will fail even when the new behavior is correct, because `_status_text` still emits `source_messages_total: ...` and that line contains the substring `messages_total:`. In other words, any unbound status output with source lineage data will trip this check, making the test fail for the wrong reason and masking the intended regression signal.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse each node_id value instead of the node_ids list**

In `lcm_expand_query`, `_parse_int_arg` always reads from `args.get(name, default)`, so calling `_parse_int_arg("node_ids", node_id)` parses the entire `node_ids` array rather than the current element. For any request that supplies `node_ids` (even valid integers like `[1, 2]`), `int(raw_node_ids)` raises `TypeError` and the function returns `{"error": "node_ids must contain only integers"}`. This regresses the explicit-node expansion path and makes `node_ids` effectively unusable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep LIKE fallback ranking from truncating arbitrary rows**

This change adds `LIMIT ?` but no `ORDER BY`, so SQLite only returns an arbitrary first slice of matches (usually low rowids) and `_fallback_result_sort_key` ranks only that subset. For fallback-triggering queries (for example hyphenated terms), better-scoring or newer matches beyond `fetch_limit` are never seen, which can return incorrect top results for `relevance`, `hybrid`, and `recency` once total matches exceed the limit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Filter DAG source matches before applying SQL LIMIT**

In DAG LIKE fallback, the new SQL `LIMIT ?` is applied before source lineage filtering (`_node_matches_source`) happens in Python, so source-scoped searches can drop valid results when early rows belong to other sources. With enough mixed-source matches, the limited window can be fully filtered out and return empty/partial results even though matching-source nodes exist later, which is a functional regression for fallback paths.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Defer strict max_tokens parsing until branch needs it**

`lcm_expand` now does `int(args.get("max_tokens", 4000))` unconditionally, so calls that include `max_tokens: null` or any non-integer string will raise before branch selection. This is a regression for `externalized_ref` and `source_type == "nodes"` flows, which previously did not depend on `max_tokens`; because `handle_tool_call` directly returns `handler(args, engine=self)` without wrapping exceptions, the tool call can fail instead of returning JSON output for otherwise valid inputs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep irreducible newest tail as best-effort context**

This unconditional `break` drops the newest tail message when it alone exceeds `assembly_cap`, which changes forced-overflow behavior from “return best-effort context and flag failure” to silently removing the latest turn. In the `compress(..., current_tokens=...)` overflow path, `_assemble_context` now returns no tail for an oversized newest message, so `_finalize_forced_overflow_result` reports `overflow_recovery_failed=False` because tokens are under cap, even though the active user/assistant turn was discarded. That regresses the irreducible overflow contract exercised by `test_forced_overflow_recovery_flags_irreducible_single_tail_overflow` in `tests/test_lcm_engine.py` and can cause replies that ignore the most recent input.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid requiring PyYAML in packaging tests**

This new test module imports `yaml` just to write a small config file, which makes `pytest` fail at collection time in environments where PyYAML is not preinstalled (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'`). Because the repository does not otherwise rely on PyYAML, this introduces an undeclared test dependency and breaks the default validation flow for clean environments.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Canonicalize paths before comparing existing symlink target**

The installer compares `readlink` output to `REPO_ROOT` as raw strings, so rerunning `install.sh` (or `update.sh`, which calls it) from the installed symlink path can fail even when both paths resolve to the same checkout. In that case `REPO_ROOT` is the symlinked path while `readlink` returns the original absolute target, and this branch incorrectly aborts with "Refusing to replace existing symlink," breaking self-update from `~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-lcm`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not split OpenRouter organization slugs as providers**

`parse_lcm_model_override` now splits any `prefix/model` when `prefix` is in `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES`, which includes names like `anthropic`; this regresses existing model-only overrides such as `anthropic/claude-*` that are valid OpenRouter-style model slugs. In that configuration, LCM auxiliary calls are rerouted from the configured provider to `provider=anthropic` with a stripped model, which can fail or hit the wrong backend when only the original provider is configured. Before this commit those values were passed through unchanged.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset state when compression carry-over is skipped**

When `boundary_reason="compression"` is present but `old_session_id` does not match the currently bound session, this path only logs a warning and then rebinds the new session without calling `_reset_session_scoped_runtime_state()`. In that mismatch case, stale per-session fields like `_ingest_cursor` and `_last_compacted_store_id` leak into the new session, so `_ingest_messages()` can skip persisting initial messages (e.g., cursor > new message list length) and silently drop storage/DAG continuity for that session. This is reachable in malformed or out-of-order boundary metadata cases, which this branch already anticipates via warning.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep externalized payloads readable after session reassignment**

This update rewrites `messages.session_id` across a compression boundary, but externalized tool-result payload files still retain their original `session_id`; downstream retrieval (`tools._get_externalized_payload` / `find_externalized_payload_for_message`) filters payloads by current session, so moved messages can no longer resolve their externalized metadata/content after rollover. As a result, `lcm_expand` loses access to large tool outputs for sessions with externalization enabled, even though the commit intends logical session continuity.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep store content shape compatible with compaction ID matching**

Serializing non-string `msg["content"]` to JSON here changes persisted multimodal messages from list/dict objects into strings, but compaction still matches raw messages to stored rows via direct equality in `LCMEngine._get_store_ids_for_messages` (`engine.py`, `(stored.get("content") or "") == content`). For content-part lists this never matches, so summary nodes lose those `source_ids` and `_last_compacted_store_id` can drop to `0` when a compacted chunk is all multimodal blocks, which breaks lineage and can mis-associate future compactions with old rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve standalone tool results in mixed tool-call chunks**

The new orphan filter drops any `tool` message whose `tool_call_id` is not in `matched_tool_ids` whenever *any* assistant tool-call ID exists in the chunk. In mixed histories, this removes legitimate standalone/legacy tool outputs (with their own IDs) just because an unrelated matched tool call is present, so compaction summaries can lose important evidence from prior steps. This is a regression from the previous behavior (which serialized all tool results) and can silently reduce recall quality for sessions that combine modern paired calls with older unpaired tool-result records.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Thanks, this was a real edge case. I reproduced it with a failing regression for a mixed chunk containing one modern matched tool-call/result pair plus a standalone legacy tool result with its own id.

Updated the branch so the cleanup no longer treats tool-result messages as orphan candidates. The serializer now:
- drops unmatched assistant `tool_calls` metadata when there is no matching tool result
- keeps matched tool-call/result pairs
- preserves standalone/legacy tool results, even in mixed chunks

Re-ran validation locally:
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` → `281 passed`
- `python -m pytest -q` → `306 passed`
- `python -m compileall -q .`
- `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh`
- `git diff --check`
- runtime smoke through the active plugin path also confirms standalone legacy tool results are preserved while empty/ACK-like/orphaned assistant tool-call metadata is omitted from summarizer serialization.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep repair scan read-only by avoiding rebuild probe**

`/lcm doctor repair` is documented as read-only, but `external_content_fts_needs_repair()` now delegates to `_fts_needs_rebuild()`, which performs an FTS `integrity-check` via `INSERT` and therefore requires write permissions. In read-only database contexts (or any connection opened `mode=ro`), this raises `OperationalError` and gets interpreted as `needs_repair=True`, producing a false repair-needed result and violating the dry-run contract.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Good catch — this was valid.

I split the dry-run diagnostic path away from the write-capable rebuild probe. `/lcm doctor repair` now uses only structural/table/count/trigger checks, so it no longer runs the FTS5 `integrity-check` INSERT and works correctly with a read-only SQLite connection. The startup/apply repair path still uses the deeper write-capable integrity check before rebuilding.

Added regression coverage:
- `test_lcm_doctor_repair_dry_run_works_with_read_only_database`

Validation after the fix:
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_command.py -q` → `28 passed`
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_lcm_command.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` → `306 passed`
- `python -m pytest -q` → `306 passed`
- `python -m compileall -q .`
- `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh`
- `git diff --check`
- runtime smoke via active plugin path confirmed read-only repair diagnostics report healthy FTS as `ok` without false `repair-needed`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset cache usage fields on session boundary**

Expose-only status fields here are session-scoped, but they are never cleared in either `_reset_session_scoped_runtime_state` or `on_session_reset`, so after switching from session A to session B (before B receives its first response) `get_status()` can report A's `last_input_tokens`/cache counters and `cache_metrics_available` as if they belonged to B. This creates incorrect operator telemetry for common `/lcm status` and `lcm_status` checks right after a rebind/reset.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Good catch, this was valid. I updated the shared session scoped reset path so cache usage counters and `cache_metrics_available` are cleared on both explicit reset and new session binding.

I also extended the existing session reset tests to cover these cache fields, including the stale status case before a new session receives its first response.

Validation from the updated head:

`python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestEngineABC::test_session_reset tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestEngineABC::test_on_session_start_resets_session_scoped_runtime_when_binding_new_session -q`

Result: `2 passed`

`python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py -q`

Result: `136 passed`

`python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q`

Result: `279 passed`

`python -m pytest -q`

Result: `306 passed`

CI is green on 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect carry_over_context in compression rollover path**

When `rollover_session(..., carry_over_context=False, boundary_reason="compression")` is used, this early branch still executes and routes through `on_session_start(..., boundary_reason="compression")`, which reassigns session messages/nodes as a continuation. That bypasses the function’s own carry-over guard and changes behavior from “no carry-over” to full state transfer, which can leak prior-session context in integrations that disable carry-over via this flag.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count message sessions against all lifecycle references**

`get_fragmentation_stats()` treats any message session not equal to a `current_session_id` as missing, but a healthy rollover intentionally leaves prior message sessions referenced via `last_finalized_session_id`. After a normal `/new` rollover, `message_sessions_without_lifecycle_current` will be >0 even when lifecycle metadata is consistent, and `_has_lifecycle_fragmentation()` in doctor/status paths escalates this to a warning. This creates systematic false-positive fragmentation warnings in valid multi-session histories.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve unknown dirty state when git probe fails**

When `_git("status", ...)` fails (e.g., `git` missing, timeout, subprocess error), `_git` returns an empty string and `plugin_git_dirty` is computed as `bool(dirty_output)`, which becomes `False`. In that failure mode, status/doctor output incorrectly reports the checkout as clean rather than unavailable, which can mislead operators trying to verify what code is running. This path is reachable whenever `.git` exists but git commands cannot be executed successfully.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Good catch. Fixed in 42e0893 so a failed git probe leaves `plugin_git_dirty` as unavailable instead of clean, with regression coverage.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear auxiliary flag on any non-aux session start**

When a live child is detected, `on_session_start` sets a thread-local auxiliary marker, but the non-aux path only calls `_clear_thread_context_stateless(session_id)`, which clears **only if** the new `session_id` matches the stored auxiliary id. If the auxiliary session does not emit a matching `on_session_end` (for example, aborted/cancelled child work) and another normal session starts on that thread, the marker remains set and `should_compress`, `should_compress_preflight`, `compress`, and tool-ingest paths keep behaving as stateless for unrelated foreground sessions. This causes persistent loss of LCM ingestion/compaction until process restart or an exact-id clear.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in ce35eff. Normal non-aux session starts now clear any stale thread-local auxiliary marker, with regression coverage for the aborted-child path.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear stale auxiliary marker before compression rollover**

If an auxiliary child session starts but never emits a matching `on_session_end`, `auxiliary_session_id` remains set in thread-local state. In `on_session_start`, the compression-boundary fast path returns immediately via `_continue_compression_boundary(...)`, so it skips the later `_clear_thread_context_stateless()` call in the normal path. As a result, the new foreground continuation session stays marked auxiliary, and `should_compress*`, `compress`, and tool-call ingestion continue to bypass persistence/compaction for that real session.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in dd53e0a. Compression-boundary starts now clear any stale auxiliary marker before the fast path returns, with regression coverage for that path.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep auxiliary marker until that child session actually ends**

Clearing the thread-local auxiliary marker before `_continue_compression_boundary(...)` means a still-running auxiliary child can later hit `on_session_end` as if it were a normal session: once the marker is cleared, the `session_id` guard at `on_session_end` no longer matches and the child’s messages are ingested/finalized into the foreground lifecycle. This is reproducible when a background child starts, a foreground compression rollover happens, and the child ends afterward; it corrupts LCM isolation by persisting auxiliary traffic.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve all active auxiliary session ids per thread**

The thread-local state stores only one `auxiliary_session_id`, so a second auxiliary child start overwrites the first child id. If the first child ends while the second id is stored, `on_session_end` misses the auxiliary guard and ingests/finalizes that first child as normal session data. In environments where multiple background children can overlap on one thread, this breaks the intended stateless isolation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in c5e2771. Active auxiliary ids now stay tracked until their own `on_session_end`, while foreground compression clears only the current stateless marker. The late child-end case has regression coverage.

Fixed in c5e2771. Thread-local auxiliary state now tracks a set of active child session ids, so overlapping child endings are handled independently. Added regression coverage for two overlapping auxiliary children.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track auxiliary session ends across threads**

This guard only works when `on_session_end()` runs on the same thread that marked the child as auxiliary in `on_session_start()`. Because auxiliary IDs are stored in `threading.local`, a session-end callback on another worker thread will miss the marker, fall through, and persist/finalize the child against the foreground binding, which reintroduces the session-corruption path this change is trying to prevent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid treating historical child sessions as live auxiliary**

The fallback branch `child_started_at < parent_ended_at` marks a child as auxiliary even when the parent is already ended, but it never checks whether the child itself is still live. Any historical child session that started before its parent ended will satisfy this forever, so resuming/reopening that session later can be misclassified as auxiliary and skipped from normal LCM binding/persistence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 73648ad. Active auxiliary session ids are now engine-wide and lock-protected, while only the current stateless marker remains thread-local. Added cross-thread `on_session_end` regression coverage.

Fixed in 73648ad. The live-child probe now requires the child row itself to still be live, so historical child sessions can bind and persist normally. Added regression coverage for reopening an ended child session.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check active auxiliary set in stateless guard**

`_thread_context_stateless()` only reads a thread-local marker, while auxiliary liveness is tracked process-wide in `_auxiliary_session_ids` for `on_session_end()`. If a live auxiliary session continues on a different worker thread (or after its local marker was cleared by a foreground start), `should_compress_preflight`, `compress`, and tool-call ingestion will treat it as a normal session and persist/compact background messages into the foreground binding. This breaks the isolation this change is introducing for overlapping child sessions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 939d1de. The stateless guard now validates the thread-local marker against the engine-wide active auxiliary set, so markers stop suppressing once another thread has ended that child. Added regression coverage for the stale-marker path.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip boundary rollover for active auxiliary child sessions**

The `boundary_reason == "compression"` fast path returns before the auxiliary-child check, so a live auxiliary child that rolls over (old child session -> new child session) is processed as a normal compression boundary. In that case `old_session_id` will not match the bound foreground `_session_id`, and `_continue_compression_boundary()` can fall back to the currently bound session as the carry-over source, finalizing/reassigning foreground messages and DAG state into the auxiliary continuation.
